entries.clue: When Democrat finally cuts state food (5)

indicators.note: takes the final letter of 'Democrat'
AS and T cut into PA, sitting inside it

blocks.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

annotation.surface: An American politician slashes a state's food budget.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'cuts' as spending cuts; here it means cutting into PA.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: pasta is one kind of food, so the broad word stands for the specific one.

entries.clue: Possibly Le Pen's report on university schedule (8)

indicators.note: 'possibly' says Le Pen is just one example of the answer, not a synonym for it

blocks.note: a report is a bang, a pop

annotation.surface: A French politician's report on a university timetable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Report' pretends to be a document; it is the sound of a gun. Marine Le Pen is the French far-right leader.
annotation.definitionFit: Le Pen is a well-known populist politician, so she is a possible example.

entries.clue: Press going after Sun? Piss off! (5)

indicators.note: something going after another follows it, so CRAM comes after S

annotation.surface: A tabloid journalist chasing the Sun gets told where to go.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Press' and 'Sun' suggest newspapers (The Sun is a British tabloid); they are a verb and a day.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Scram!' and 'Piss off!' are both rude orders to go away.

entries.clue: He's also mistaken for a scumbag (7)

indicators.note: the letters of HE'S ALSO are got wrong, rearranged

annotation.surface: A man is also wrongly taken for a lowlife.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'mistaken for' as one idea; 'mistaken' works on the words before it and 'for a' just links.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are coarse insults for a contemptible person.

entries.clue: Far-reaching organisation's reckless cop-out against society (7)

indicators.note: COP-OUT is rearranged recklessly
S is placed next to the anagram

annotation.surface: A sprawling organisation dodges its responsibilities to society.
annotation.walkthrough: An octopus is a figurative name for an organisation with tentacles everywhere.
annotation.definitionFit: An organisation reaching into many areas is called an octopus, after its many arms.

entries.clue: Not an item of underwear for Balls to adorn (9)

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

annotation.surface: A remark that some garment is not suitable underwear for Ed Balls to wear.
annotation.walkthrough: Ed Balls is a British Labour politician, but here balls are cricket deliveries. The definition is cryptic: an overdress is worn over other clothes, the opposite of underwear.
annotation.definitionFit: An overdress is a dress worn over another garment, so it is outerwear rather than underwear.

entries.clue: In fact, her most useful means of keeping things hot? (7)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A question about the handiest way to keep something warm.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across three words, ignoring the comma.
annotation.definitionFit: A Thermos flask keeps drinks hot.

entries.clue: PM misses out, having to accept one negative world view (9)

indicators.note: PM MISSES is knocked out of shape, rearranged
to accept something is to take it in, so the mix takes I inside it

blocks.note: Roman numeral one, taken into the mix

annotation.surface: A prime minister misses out and must settle for a gloomy outlook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Misses out' looks like a phrase; 'out' belongs to the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an outlook that always expects the worst is the negative way of seeing the world.

entries.clue: It conveys an expression of disappointment about gutless Labourite (6)

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so SIGH is wrapped around LE
Labourite loses its insides, leaving L and E

annotation.surface: Someone sighs at a spineless Labour Party member.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It conveys' looks like the start of the wordplay but is the definition: a sleigh carries people.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: 'it conveys' describes what the thing does, carrying people and goods over snow.

entries.clue: see 12ac. (4)
Cries off intervening in pontiff's means of overlooking the crowd (9)

indicators.note: CRIES goes off, rearranged
the anagram goes inside POPE

annotation.surface: Shouts of protest interrupt the Pope as he looks out over the faithful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cries off' looks like 'backs out'; 'off' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A periscope lets you see over the heads of a crowd.

entries.clue: Follow Eye – never starts to instigate a lawsuit (5)

indicators.note: take the starting letters of 'Eye' and 'never'

blocks.note: first letters of Eye and Never
to sue is to bring a lawsuit

annotation.surface: Private Eye vows never to be the one who starts legal action.
annotation.walkthrough: Private Eye, the magazine this puzzle appears in, is famously sued for libel, which makes the surface a joke on itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of coming next as a result, as trouble follows a bad decision.

entries.clue: Knock shit and briefly ridicule (7)

blocks.note: to lam is to hit hard
'n' is short for 'and', as in rock 'n' roll

annotation.surface: Hit something foul and quickly mock it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knock' pretends to mean criticise, which is close to the definition; it is LAM, a hit.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the verb means mocking someone publicly, usually in satirical writing.

entries.clue: (& 8dn.) At a loss for words with elected government head and wretched diluting of intellectual content (7)

blocks.note: a party that is elected is in

annotation.surface: A speechless new government leader presides over a miserable slide in public debate.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 8 down. 'Government head' gives only G, its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Dumbing down is making something less intellectually demanding.

entries.clue: Receives jolt, admitting Trump's lead is close (9)

indicators.note: RECEIVES is jolted into a new order
to admit is to let in, so the mix lets T inside
the leading letter of Trump

blocks.note: first letter of Trump, taken into the mix

annotation.surface: Someone gets a shock when admitting that Trump's lead is narrow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like 'narrow' in the surface; it means tight-lipped. 'Jolt' works as an anagram signal on the word before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A close person keeps things to themselves, that is, is secretive.

entries.clue: Labour finished off somewhat unnaturally by such a section? (9)

definitions.text: Labour finished off somewhat unnaturally by such a section?

blocks.note: read as a political party brought down, and meant as childbirth ended by a doctor rather than by nature
read as a faction within the party, and meant as a surgical cut

annotation.surface: A section of the Labour Party brings things to an unnatural end.
annotation.walkthrough: Labour pretends to be the political party; it is childbirth, and the section is surgical, not a party faction.
annotation.definitionFit: A Caesarean section delivers a baby by surgery instead of natural labour.

entries.clue: Stick one on irate Ben, useless piss-artist (9)

indicators.note: in a down answer, I is placed on top of what follows
IRATE BEN is made useless, rearranged

annotation.surface: An order to punch an angry, hopeless drunk called Ben.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stick one on' is slang for punching someone; here it just places I above the rest. A piss-artist is British slang for a habitual drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional slang match: piss-artist is British slang for a habitual drunk, which is what the formal noun means.

entries.clue: see 24dn. (4)
Lacking experience, starts to tipple exceedingly alcoholic beverage (5,3)

indicators.note: take the starting letters of the next three words

blocks.note: first letters of Tipple, Exceedingly, Alcoholic

annotation.surface: A novice drinker begins on something very strong.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface promises booze; the answer is about as far from exceedingly alcoholic as a drink gets.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the answer is one kind of beverage, unfermented tea leaves brewed in hot water.

entries.clue: (& 23ac.) Remark tires out follower of Corbyn (4)

indicators.note: REMARK TIRES is put out of order

annotation.surface: A comment wears out one of Jeremy Corbyn's supporters.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 23 across. 'Follower' means successor: Starmer followed Corbyn as Labour leader, though hardly as his disciple.
annotation.definitionFit: Keir Starmer succeeded Jeremy Corbyn as leader of the Labour Party.

entries.clue: You'll be sorry feeling that after, er, getting erection, end of todger is in some distress (7)

definitions.text: You'll be sorry feeling that after
definitions.note: a descriptive definition: remorse is the sorry feeling you have afterwards

indicators.note: in a down answer, ER is raised upright, reading upwards
take the last letter of 'todger'
R goes inside the anagram
SOME is distressed, rearranged

blocks.note: last letter of todgeR, placed inside MOSE

annotation.surface: A cautionary tale about embarrassment after an ill-timed arousal.
annotation.walkthrough: Todger is British slang for penis. 'Erection' is the smutty reversal signal: in a down clue the letters are stood up.
annotation.definitionFit: Remorse is regret felt after doing something.

entries.clue: Country is raging at Tories raking in millions (4,5)

indicators.note: AT TORIES rages into a new order
raking in money means gathering it up, so the mix gathers M inside

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, taken into the mix

annotation.surface: A nation is furious at Conservatives pocketing millions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is raging' reads as one phrase; 'is' just links and 'raging' shuffles the next two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the answer is one particular country, the Southeast Asian state also called Timor-Leste.

entries.clue: Trial dubious? F-off and provide the evidence! (7)

indicators.note: read literally, 'F off' means take an F off, so IFFY loses one F

annotation.surface: A defendant scorns a dodgy trial and tells the court to prove it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'F-off' reads as the swear word; it is an instruction to drop an F.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the courtroom: a witness who takes the stand does exactly this.

entries.clue: Whispers from presidential staff about 'sexual initiation' (6)

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so AIDES is wrapped around S
the start of 'sexual', its first letter

annotation.surface: White House staff gossip about someone's first sexual experience.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initiation' pretends to be a rite of passage; it asks only for the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Asides are remarks spoken quietly, as whispers.

entries.clue: see 18ac. (7)
Bush needs Scholz's agreement – and that of Cyclops – to admit son (7)

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so JA and MINE let S in between them

blocks.note: German for yes; Olaf Scholz is a German politician
Cyclops is the setter, so what is his is 'mine'

annotation.surface: A US President Bush needs the German chancellor's backing, and the setter's, to bring in his son.
annotation.walkthrough: Bush pretends to be the president; it is a shrub.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the answer is one kind of bush, the climbing shrub with scented white flowers.

entries.clue: (& 16ac.) Nothing produced by white balls? Slap! (4)

blocks.note: in lawn bowls the jack is the small white target ball

annotation.surface: A snooker or bowls mishap: the white balls produce nothing, so someone lashes out.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 16 across. The wordplay splits across the enumeration: the S of the plural belongs to the second word.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the crude American phrase means nothing at all, as in 'he knows diddly-squat'.

entries.clue: Fancy Lanvin's top model (5)

indicators.note: the top of Lanvin, in a down answer its first letter

blocks.note: a fancy is a notion, an idea

annotation.surface: An exclamation of admiration for a Lanvin catwalk model.
annotation.walkthrough: Lanvin is a Paris fashion house, so 'top model' reads as a catwalk star; 'top' takes one letter and 'model' is an exemplar.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of a perfect example others copy, as in 'a model pupil'.

entries.clue: Dull and tedious Democrat at bottom (5)

annotation.surface: A boring Democrat who comes last.
annotation.walkthrough: Drear is a literary form of dreary.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary synonym: the poetic short form of dreary covers both halves of the definition.

entries.clue: Designer chic: treat as perverted (9)

indicators.note: CHIC TREAT is turned from its proper order

annotation.surface: Fashion stylishness dismissed as something kinky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Designer chic' reads as a fashion phrase; 'Designer' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the answer is the professional who draws up plans for buildings.

entries.clue: Frank, after that time with redneck extremist leaders (7)

indicators.note: the leading letters of 'redneck' and 'extremist'

blocks.note: since means from that time on
first letters of Redneck and Extremist

annotation.surface: Someone called Frank, who has since joined the leaders of far-right rednecks.
annotation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name; it means honest. A redneck is a US term for a reactionary rural white person.
annotation.definitionFit: Frank and sincere both mean honest and open.

entries.clue: One time sexual partner's back in conference venue (5)

indicators.note: A, T and LAY read backwards

annotation.surface: A former lover turns up again at a conference.

annotation.definitionFit: Yalta hosted the 1945 conference of Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin.
